diagram_math_checks.justification: The supplier Definition places inputs above outputs. A has one top and three bottom vertices, paired as {input,n1},{n2,n3}; B has {n1,p1},{n2,p2},{n3,p3}; C has {p1,output},{p2,p3}. Each is a perfect matching, hence also a partition basis diagram. Codomains 3 and 3 match the next domains.

After gluing the two numbered interfaces there are eight vertices and seven graph edges. The outer path input–n1–p1–output has three edges. K is the explicit closed four-edge circuit n2–n3–p3–p2–n2, rendered with two curved caps and two vertical edges. Six internal vertices have degree two; the two outer vertices have degree one. Dashed horizontal guide rows are expressly excluded from graph edges.

For B∘A, the cap n2–n3 becomes the output cap p2–p3 and no class is removed; composition with C closes K. For C∘B, the bottom cap becomes the input cap n2–n3 and no class is removed; composition with A closes K. Thus removed counts are 0+1 in both orders, and the retained outer matching is id_1. Supplier composition and proof steps 1.1–3.1 give delta id_1.

Original proof steps 1.1–3.1 remain byte-identical and prove the general associativity and units through finite equivalence classes and bilinearity. The new Remarks explicitly describes the drawing as an illustration only.
